prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1025; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed head-on collision reported by the insured driver. Vehicle damage appears limited to front bumper assembly and hood. Claimant reports concussion symptoms and has retained legal counsel. All further contact to be routed through counsel's office. Requested police report and photos of both vehicles.

Entry 2: Police report received. Responding officer noted minor front-end damage to both vehicles, no airbag deployment, and vehicles driven from scene. Liability appears disputed on the question of lane position at impact. Scene photos reviewed and placed in file. Referred to senior adjuster for liability assessment.

Entry 3: Spoke with claimant's attorney's office. Counsel confirmed representation and requested that the claimant not be contacted directly. Medical authorization forms sent to counsel for signature. Counsel indicated the claimant was evaluated at an urgent care facility and diagnosed with a concussion. Requested copies of all treatment records and billing statements.

Entry 4: Medical records received from urgent care provider. Diagnosis recorded as mild concussion with headache, dizziness, and light sensitivity. Follow-up referral to neurology noted. Records also reference prior history of migraines, which counsel should be asked to address. Reserve reviewed and adjusted pending further medical documentation. Independent medical review under consideration.

Entry 5: Counsel's office provided updated status. Claimant remains under neurology care and reports ongoing symptoms. Settlement demand package expected once treatment concludes. Repair estimate for insured vehicle finalized and approved. Claim remains open pending liability determination and receipt of complete medical file. Diary set for follow-up with counsel's office.
